title: Who Do You Want to Be?

howDoI.q: How do I make a door that picks the hero?
How do I send two doors to two different scenes?
How do I make a scene load a different character file?
How do I make one hero walk faster than another?
How do I make one hero jump higher than another?
How do I keep the hero I picked in a later scene?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Who Do You Want to Be? is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into a door to go through it.

Play it twice, once through each door. Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: Two Doors
pages.html:
Level 1: Two Doors

You start in the middle of a small room. FAST FEET. RUNS QUICKLY, JUMPS LIKE LIAN is by the door on the left. BIG HOPS. SLOW FEET, JUMPS SIX BLOCKS is by the door on the right. TWO DOORS, TWO HEROES. THE SAME LEVEL BEHIND BOTH stands between them. Take the coins, read the signs and walk into a door. Both lead to the same climb, so you can come back and pick the other one.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Two links. Open pick.gam in the Scenes tab and select the room. A scene can have several links: a block-sized spot on the map, and the scene it takes the hero to. Here the left door's spot goes to the Fast Feet climb and the right door's spot goes to the Big Hops climb.
  • The doors are ordinary blocks. The link is not drawn: the door picture is just a block on top of the spot. Nothing in the map says which door is which, so the signs do.
  • The room's hero. The room itself loads fast.chr, Lian's own file, so you walk it as Fast Feet.
  • The map. Open doors.map: a flat floor, a hedge at each end, the entrance in the middle and a door at each end. The coins are at head height so that walking collects them.

pages.head: Level 2: The Same Climb
pages.html:
Level 2: The Same Climb

The climb is two steps up to a plateau, then a drop and the exit. STEPS UP. EVERY HERO CAN TAKE THEM and BIG HOPS CAN SKIP A STEP. FAST FEET TAKES THEM ALL are the first signs. Fast Feet walks up both steps. Big Hops can hop from the ground onto the second step and skip the first. HIGH COINS NEED BIG HOPS. TRY THE OTHER DOOR is on the plateau, under three coins that only Big Hops can reach. Take the other coins and walk into the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • One map, two scenes. In pick.gam there are two scenes that load climb.map, one called Climb: Fast Feet and one called Climb: Big Hops. The only difference between them is two slots in the scene's file list: the character and its character blocks (fast.chr and fast.cbl, or hops.chr and hops.cbl).
  • What makes Big Hops different. Open hops.chr in the Character tab. The Space sequence starts with a bigger push upward (17, not 12), and each walking frame moves the hero 3 pixels instead of Fast Feet's 6. The pictures are the same ones with a purple hoodie.
  • Sized by the map. Fast Feet jumps a little over three blocks, so each step is only one or two blocks higher than the last. Big Hops jumps six, which clears the first step and, from the plateau, reaches the coins that hang high above it.
  • The exit. Both climb scenes link their door to the The End scene in pick.gam.

pages.head: Level 3: The Open Road
pages.html:
Level 3: The Open Road

After the climb comes a short road with one hill. NO HERO IS SET HERE: YOU ARE STILL THE ONE YOU PICKED stands at the start. Walk, hop the hill and take the coins to the exit door. Fast Feet gets there sooner and Big Hops takes the hill in a bounce, but nobody is stopped: nothing on the road needs a particular hero.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • One blank slot. Open pick.gam in the Scenes tab and select The Open Road. Its character and character blocks slots are empty. Every other file is named as usual.
  • What the engine does with a blank slot. PLAYGAME loads each scene file only if its name is set (code/GM/PLAYGAME.C lines 4252 and 4253: if (Game.FileExists(scnum,5)) ... loadspecany(... &chr), then the same for slot 6, the character blocks). The test is at code/GM/GRATOR.H line 233: a name that is zero means no file. With nothing to load, the character already in memory is kept, with its sequences and pictures. The web player does the same in web/packages/engine/src/engine/scene.ts lines 156 and 162: chr ? parseCharacter(chr) : prev!.chr.
  • The link in. Both climb scenes link their door to this scene instead of straight to The End, so it follows whichever hero you picked.
  • The map. Open road.map: a flat road, a two-block step and a three-block hill, all things that Fast Feet and Big Hops can both walk up. Nothing is hero-only, so nobody gets stuck.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot choose a hero from what you did. A scene loads the character file it names, or none. A blank slot keeps the last hero, as the road does, but nothing chooses between two files from a counter. To have two heroes through the same level, make a scene for each hero, as the climb has.
  • A saved game can lose the hero. Loading a save straight into a scene with no character file has no hero to keep. Give any scene you may load into its own character file.
  • It cannot change the hero inside a scene. The character file is loaded once, when the scene starts. To change who you are, go through a link to another scene.
  • One file holds all of a hero's moves. A hero is one file: its sequences, its pictures and its counters. A second hero is a second file, and any move they share has to be made twice.
  • A door is a link. It cannot be switched on or off, and nothing marks which door is which except what you draw.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Open hops.chr and make the push on the Space sequence bigger. How high can a hero go before the map's edge stops them?
  • Change a scene's character slot to the other hero's file, and play that door again.
  • Name hops.chr in the road's character slot and see the road stop following your pick.
  • Add a third door to the room, a third scene, and a third character file with your own numbers.
  • Draw a new hoodie color in hops.cbl.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
